title: Manicotti
subtitle: Italian-American crêpe manicotti with ricotta and tomato
excerpt: Large crêpes filled with ricotta, egg, and mozzarella, rolled, arranged in a baking dish with tomato sauce, and baked with more sauce and Parmesan. The Italian-American version uses crêpes rather than dried pasta tubes.
sourceNotes: Manicotti is an Italian-American dish that uses large crêpes (rather than the dried pasta tubes sometimes sold as manicotti in Italy) to wrap a ricotta filling, then bakes them in tomato sauce. The crêpe version is the traditional Italian-American approach, documented in multiple mid-twentieth-century Italian-American cookbooks. The dish is associated with Sunday dinner and Italian-American holiday cooking in the northeast United States.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble the dish but do not bake. Freeze covered in the baking dish. Defrost overnight in the fridge and bake from room temperature as normal.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The crêpes can be made 2 days ahead and stacked interleaved with baking paper. The assembled dish can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours before baking.

content.text: Italian-American manicotti uses crêpes, not dried pasta tubes: thin, lacy pancakes made just rich enough to roll around a ricotta filling. The crêpe absorbs the tomato sauce as the dish bakes, and the result is softer and more delicate than the pasta-tube version. This is Sunday dinner food: something that takes time to make and is worth every minute of it.
Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, and salt into a smooth batter. Leave to rest for 30 minutes. Cook 12 thin, 20 cm crêpes in a lightly buttered pan. Stack on a plate and set aside.
For the sauce: heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, season, and simmer for 20 minutes until slightly thickened.
Mix the ricotta, chopped mozzarella, 2 eggs, 50 g Parmesan, and parsley together. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce across the base of a large baking dish.

Place 2 heaped tablespoons of filling along the centre of each crêpe. Roll the crêpe around the filling and place seam-side down in the baking dish. Repeat with the remaining crêpes, arranging them snugly side by side.
Pour the remaining tomato sauce over the crêpes. Scatter with the remaining Parmesan. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Batter too thick or crêpes too thin and fragile
items.fix: The batter should be thin enough to swirl easily in the pan. Crêpes need to be large enough (20 cm) to roll without cracking.

items.cause: Too much filling, or seams facing up
items.fix: Keep the filling to 2 tablespoons per crêpe and place seam-side down.

content.text: Manicotti is Italian-American Sunday food, made in homes across New York and New Jersey from the early twentieth century onwards. The crêpe version is the original method. The dried pasta tube version is a later shortcut. On the Sunday table, manicotti sits alongside salad, bread, and braised meatballs or sausage. It feeds a crowd and holds well on a buffet.
